articles.title: Paging Hezbollah? Exposing Israel’s terrorist pager attack on Lebanon | w/ Radwan Mortada
articles.author: Rania Khalek
articles.content_excerpt: Two years after Israel’s pager attacks on Lebanon killed dozens and maimed thousands, Lebanese investigative journalist Radwan Mortada’s new two-part Al Jazeera documentary, The Trap (Al-Mesyada), goes inside the September 2024 Mossad operation more than a decade in the making. Mortada joins Rania Khalek to trace the web of front companies stretching from Taiwan to Bulgaria that enabled Israel to infiltrate Gold Apollo, a supplier Hezbollah had trusted for decades. As a new Israeli propaganda film Paging Hezbollah heads for US theaters, Mortada reveals that Israel’s goal to kill as many as 20,000 Hezbollah fighters with booby-trapped walkie-talkies, in fact, fell far short. articles.title: Brazil bans online betting
articles.content_excerpt: The impasse is over. After days of uncertainty over what Brazil should do about online betting, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government announced Friday in São Paulo that sports betting houses will be shut down nationwide. Online casinos, including gambling games such as Tigrinho , are banned as well. The bans on bets and online casinos took effect immediately. Lula is also expected to send Congress a bill establishing penalties for anyone who operates, runs, or promotes betting. The move came through a decree signed by Lula, which took effect right away. Finance Minister Dario Durigan made the announcement and explained the reasoning. “Our decision stems from the harmful effect that bets have had in Brazil,” Durigan said. articles.title: Lula and Trump Defend Opposing World Views at UN General Assembly
articles.content_excerpt: The two main speeches at the opening of the U.N. General Assembly were delivered by Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and U.S. President Donald Trump. The leaders addressed many of the same issues, but their speeches offered sharply contrasting visions of the global order. Sérgio Costa, a sociology professor at the Free University of Berlin, described Lula’s speech as important and forceful, not only for its defense of multilateralism, but also for the statesmanship Lula displayed in his address. “I think Lula made this very clear: multilateralism is essential to global health, for example. articles.title: ‘Cut ties with Palantir’, say UK’s health workers
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: On Thursday, October 1, health workers, patients, and activists protested Palantir’s role in the National Health Service (NHS) at more than 40 locations across England. Their demonstrations were part of a global week of action demanding that governments cut ties with the spy-tech firm over human rights and privacy concerns. articles.title: Israel to divide central West Bank with settler-only highway
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: In late September, Israeli media reported that Netanyahu’s government intends to adjust access to key routes in the central West Bank. It plans to reopen Route 463 to settler-only traffic in the governorate of Ramallah and Al-Bireh. Yisrael Gantz , the leader of the Yesha Council (an umbrella organization representing Israeli municipal councils across Israeli settlements in the West Bank and the Jordan Valley) confirmed that plans to reopen the road received preliminary approval and funding. Preparations are also underway by the Israeli military to complete “the security, legal, and logistical” steps required to reopen the route (also known as Wallerstein Road).
